_about: Signal Box questions, copied once from the Ethical Considerations in AI guide (https://tidyweb.github.io/ethical-considerations-in-ai/#screening-tool) on 20 October 2026. A fixed record for this project; it is not updated from the guide.

qs.q: Will it make or shape a decision that matters to someone's life: work, money, care, safety, liberty?
Could a simpler non-AI process do the job?
Is the purpose vague, or likely to grow beyond what was agreed?
Does most of the benefit go to the organisation while the cost falls on others?
Does it collect or use information about identifiable people?
Is that information used automatically to evaluate or predict something about someone (profiling)?
Does it use sensitive data (health, ethnicity, biometrics, religion, sexuality) or a stand-in for it, like a postcode?
Could people be re-identified by combining fields, even with names removed?
Is any data's origin, accuracy or permission to use unknown?
Are some groups missing or thin in the data?
Is the system learning from past human decisions, such as who was hired before?
Is a consequential decision made without meaningful human involvement (solely automated)?
Would a human reviewer lack the time, information or authority to overrule it?
Is the output likely to be treated as proof rather than a prompt (automation bias)?
Could errors fall more heavily on some groups than others?
Could people be affected without knowing AI was involved?
Would an affected person be unable to understand, correct or challenge the result?
Were the people affected left out of design and testing?
Does it change anyone's job, pace of work or level of monitoring?
Could a failure cause physical or psychological harm?
Has it only been tested in a demo or lab, not the real setting?
Is there no tested way to pause it, override it or switch to a manual fallback?
Could it be attacked, misused or used outside its intended purpose?
Is there no named person who owns it, monitors it and can stop it?
Does it depend on a supplier's model, data or updates you can't inspect?
Does the EU AI Act class its intended use as high-risk?
Will it be used in a different country, population or language from the one it was built for?
